title: Locate draft takes a viewport release in the frame its page is hidden (pre-dock drop, after #566 + #668)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**A locate draft can take a viewport release in the same frame its page is hidden.**

#566 (7338fbd4) drops a locate draft whose form wasn't drawn, via `locate_pick::sweep`, which runs **after** the dock.

**The gap** (found by the #668 work):
- a viewport pick fires on mouse **release**;
- a layout change that hides the Properties pane applies **before** the dock (`layout::settle`). A keyboard panel toggle while the button is held does it;
- so the press lands while the form is shown and the release lands in the frame the page is hidden. The viewport routes that release to the still-live draft before the sweep runs.

**Fix:**
- once #668 (`layout::is_shown`, plus the pre-dock `disarm_all` for setup picks) and #566 are both on main, add the locate draft to #668's **pre-dock** check: if Properties isn't shown, drop `locate_pick` too;
- pin it with #668's same-frame test shape (`a_click_in_the_frame_the_pane_hides_misses_the_hidden_draft`), using a locate draft.

**Done means:** that test, written for a locate draft, fails without the pre-dock drop and passes with it.

Depends on #566 and #668.

title: Plasma: verification laws for through-cuts - kerf crossing, cut order, rapids, 2D gouge (part of #621)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**Plasma verification laws: what replaces the gouge and collision checks for a through-cut.**

From [UM10720](https://tormach.com/media/asset/u/m/um10720_1300pl_1223a_web.pdf) §1.4.2, §4.12.8, §4.13 and the LinuxCNC Plasma Primer §12:
- **Kerf crossing.** A cut path that crosses an already-cut kerf or void (THC dives into the gap, which "can smash the torch into the material") is warned, naming the contour and point. A rapid across a cut-out part's area is warned too (tip-up hazard).
- **Cut order.** A part's inner contours must be cut before the outer that frees it. A violation is refused by name.
- **Rapids.** Rapids run at the operator's G30 Z (no CAM Z). The post must emit G30 after every M205; a missing G30 is a post bug that the law catches.
- **Kerf against the part.** The kerf-offset path must not cut into the part's material, which is the 2D gouge (part geometry versus the kerf band).
- **The 3D stock sim** doesn't run for plasma ops. The verdict is the 2D laws above, stated as such and not silently skipped.

**Done means:** each law is pinned with a fixture that trips it and one that passes; the program verdict blocks the post on a refusal (Prime Directive).

Part of #621

title: Plasma: a PathPilot plasma post for the 1300PL - M200/G15/G16/M205/G30 (part of #621)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**A PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL.**

Words from [UM10720](https://tormach.com/media/asset/u/m/um10720_1300pl_1223a_web.pdf) §6–7 and Tormach's [post guidelines](https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/8l/pathpilot-post-processor-guidelines):
- **Preamble:** `G20|G21 / G90 / G64 P<inch> / G17 / G54.. / G43 H1 / G30`. G64 P is always in inches.
- **Per contour:** `G0` to the lead-in start, then `M200` (AutoFS; or M207/M208/M209/M210/M211 plus F when the op states them), `G15` (probe), `G16` (pierce + THC on), the XY `G1`/`G2`/`G3` path, `M205` (torch off and back to G30 Z), `G30`.
- **End:** `G30` then `M30`.
- **Refused by name:** M3/M4/M5/M7/M8/M9, any Z cutting move, G95/G96.
- **M6 conflict:** the manual's example uses `T1 M6`, but the guidelines list M6 as unsupported on plasma. It's resolved by **omitting M6** and noting it, pending a Hub or real-machine run.
- **No program delimiters** (`%`).

**Done means:**
- the post writes the per-contour block exactly;
- refusals are pinned;
- a golden `.nc` exists for a plate with an outer profile and two holes;
- a PathPilot Hub (1300PL) run is requested from the contributor before trusting it on a machine.

Part of #621

title: Plasma: a 2D through-cut profile operation - kerf, leads, cut direction, small holes, inner-first (part of #621)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**A plasma profile operation: a 2D through-cut with kerf, leads, cut direction and small-hole rules.**

- **Geometry:** closed or open 2D contours, inner and outer, cut through with no depth stepping.
- **Kerf:** the torch's kerf width, applied in the computer (offset path). An option posts G41/G42 instead, with PathPilot's rule of a straight G1 entry longer than the tool radius ([Tormach post guidelines](https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/8l/pathpilot-post-processor-guidelines)).
- **Direction:** outside contours CW, inside CCW (Hypertherm: the square edge on the part). It's overridable, and the override is stated.
- **Leads:** an arc lead-in and lead-out by default, with lengths as parameters.
  - **Small holes:** for Ø below a threshold (default 32 mm, or under 1.5× thickness), use a perpendicular lead-in from near the centre (≤ the radius), **no lead-out**, an optional overburn, and a 60–70 % feed factor (LinuxCNC Plasma Primer §13). A 1300PL forum report links hole lead-outs to arc loss.
- **Cut order:** inner contours before their outer contour, so a part never drops before its holes are cut.
- **Parameters:** feed is optional, since M200 (AutoFS) sets it on the 1300PL. Pierce height, cut height and delay are optional; when left blank, the controller's AutoFS decides.

**Done means:**
- the op generates offset XY paths with leads in the stated directions, inner first;
- small holes take the hole rule;
- it's undoable through commands and round-trips through the project file;
- golden CL output is pinned for a plate with holes.

Part of #621

title: Plasma: a 'plasma' machine kind and the Tormach 1300PL machine file (part of #621)

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**A `plasma` machine kind, and the Tormach 1300PL machine file.**

**The kind.** A `kind: plasma` in the `.mch`:
- **Axes:** X and Y cut; Z is the torch lifter, not a depth axis.
- **No spindle:** no rpm range, no power.
- **Torch:** a torch tool (Tool 1 by convention); a kerf width replaces the tool diameter.
- **Engine behaviour:** the machine check judges XY travel and feed. Z cutting depth and rpm checks don't apply and are skipped, not failed. The stock sim's depth model doesn't fit a through-cut, so plasma ops are judged by the 2D plasma laws (the safety sub-issue) instead.

**The 1300PL**, cited from [UM10720 v1223A](https://tormach.com/media/asset/u/m/um10720_1300pl_1223a_web.pdf) §2 and the 03/24 spec sheet:
- **Travels:** X 48.5 / Y 50 / Z 3.9 in. These are the smaller of the manual's and spec sheet's figures; the conflict is recorded in the decision file.
- **Feeds:** 1000 IPM on X and Y, 120 IPM on Z.
- **Rapid:** none is published, so it's left unstated.
- **Units:** inch.
- **Post:** the PathPilot plasma post (sibling sub-issue).

**Done means:**
- the kind parses and validates, with a plasma machine refusing spindle words by name;
- the 1300PL ships as a built-in machine, pinned by a spec test like `tormach_machines`;
- `machine.rs` expectations are updated.

title: UI: recent files - the last N projects and models offered when opening

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## What

When opening a **project** (`.camproj`) or a **model** (STEP, STL, …), offer the **most recent N files**, so a re-open is one click instead of a file-dialog walk.

**Requested by** the contributor (mkinney), 2026-11-09.

**Today:** **Open** (project) and **Model** (import) both go straight to the OS file dialog (`rfd::FileDialog` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs`; `actions::open_project` and `actions::open_model_dialog`). Nothing remembers what was opened before.

## Proposed behaviour

1. **Two recent lists,** kept separately: **Recent projects** and **Recent models**. Each is newest first, de-duplicated by canonical path, and capped at **N = 10** by default (configurable in Settings, 0 to turn it off).
2. **Where they show:**
   - the toolbar's **Open** and **Model** buttons get a drop-down (or a split-button arrow) listing the recent files, with "Browse…" at the bottom opening the file dialog as today;
   - the File menu, if there is one, gets "Open Recent" submenus too.
3. **Each entry:** shows the file name, with the full path on hover. An entry whose file no longer exists is shown greyed with "(missing)" and is refused by name if clicked (never a crash). A **Clear recent** item empties the list.
4. **When a file is added:** after a successful open, import or **Save As**. A failed open isn't added.
5. **Storage:**
   - **Where:** a per-user settings file, not the project, in the OS config directory, beside any existing app settings.
   - **Bad input:** a corrupt or unreadable recents file is ignored with a logged diagnostic, never a crash.
   - **Paths:** stored as given (absolute), and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
6. **Not undoable:** opening a recent file is the same command path as opening through the dialog. The recent list itself is app preference state, not document state, so it's outside the command history (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command": ephemeral or preference UI state is not undoable).
7. **Unsaved changes:** opening a recent project while the current one has unsaved changes takes the same save-or-discard prompt as **Open** today.

## Done means

- **Lists:** both recent lists appear on the Open and Model buttons, newest first, capped and de-duplicated, with missing files greyed out and refused by name, and Clear recent works.
- **Persistence:** they survive an app restart, and a corrupt recents file starts empty with a logged warning.
- **Tests:**
  - app or UI unit tests for the list logic: add, de-dup, cap, missing file, corrupt file;
  - a UI structural test for the drop-down entries (AccessKit labels).
- No snapshot PNG changes in the PR.

title: UI: look and feel like SolidCraft's (pin its shared UI kit, per solidcraft#14399)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## Goal

**Make CamCraft's UI look and feel like SolidCraft's** (tangency-labs/solidcraft, Apache-2.0, also Rust + egui): the same window chrome, ribbon or app bar, browser tree, Preferences window, theme and accent tokens, icons and type, and the same interaction feel. A user moving between the CAD and CAM app should feel at home in both. Requested by the maintainer's contributor (mkinney), 2026-11-09.

## The model: tangency-labs/solidcraft#14399

That PR ("UI kit: no SolidCraft content; tabs, text and catalogues are host data", part of solidcraft#14251) is the pattern to follow. It turns SolidCraft's UI kit into **generic UI that a host app configures with data**:
- **Tabs and accents:** the theme crate defines accent ramps (`AccentRamp`), and the host installs its own `TabTable` (`install_tabs`) naming its tabs and the ramp each uses.
- **Host text:**
  - history-step accents, inspector and workspace-menu names, Preferences page text, theme option names;
  - the navigation bar's slot catalogue (`navigation_slots`);
  - tree row names (`install_row_names`).
- **Generic pieces:** the kit's own `chord_label`, clock and icon set.
- **Guards:** two tests forbid kit code from naming app tab, command or message ids.

**solidcraft#14251** carries it on. It extracts the kit and the app-free components as **`solidcraft-ui-kit`**, "so another app can pin them":
- **Components:** `ribbon`, `app_bar`, `prefs_window`, `start_page`, `history_bar`, `navigation_bar`, `view_compass`, `window_chrome`.
- **Done when:** a minimal example app pins only shared crates and opens a window with the app bar, ribbon and Preferences.

CamCraft would be exactly that "another app".

## Open questions (to settle before code; label `needs-research` if they grow)

1. **Pin or re-implement?**
   - **Pin (recommended once it ships):** depend on `solidcraft-ui-kit` and its siblings (`theme`, `color`, `ui-text`, `viewport-egui`…) once #14251's crate lands, and supply CamCraft's tabs, text and icons as host data the way #14399 does. It looks identical with no fork drift.
   - **Re-implement:** match the look by hand in `crates/ui`.
   - A new dependency is a maintainer decision (AGENTS.md: `needs-maintainer`). Apache-2.0 needs its NOTICE kept in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`.
2. **Layering:** AGENTS.md's ui → app → flecs rule and "Everything Is a Command" must hold. Kit components return what the user chose, and CamCraft turns that into commands. Check that none of the kit's components write state directly.
3. **What maps to what:**
   - SolidCraft's workspace tabs become CamCraft's (Setup, 2D, 3D, Drill, Turn, Multi-axis, Sim, Post…).
   - Its history bar becomes CamCraft's operation list or undo history.
   - Its browser tree becomes CamCraft's setup and operation tree.
   - Decide which components CamCraft adopts first.
4. **Icons:** CamCraft's Tabler set vs the kit's icon set. AGENTS.md's icon licence rules apply.
5. **Snapshots:** the UI pixel goldens change wholesale. They're regenerated once, at a cut (AGENTS.md "Pixel snapshots are release-lane"), and the structural twins carry the asserts.
6. **wgpu / egui versions:** CamCraft's must match the kit's, or be bumped.

## Done means

CamCraft's main window, Preferences, setup/operation tree and ribbon or app bar use SolidCraft's look and feel, through a pinned shared kit or a faithful match. Every UI change is still a command, the structural UI tests pass, and the snapshot refresh is planned for the cut. The breakdown is filed as sub-issues if this is taken as research first.

## Contacts

For questions about SolidCraft's kit or #14399/#14251, ask **nateuax** or **jyviko** on Discord (their Discord names, not GitHub logins).

title: Lathe tool orientation numbers depend on the turret side: PathPilot (rear tool, X+ toward the tool) numbers a standard OD tool 3, not 2

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: This will not be worked on

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found in M5's review of #640 (#630), which reads the LinuxCNC 1-9 orientation chart in its front-tool-lathe frame: standard OD tool = 2, tip offset (-X, -Z) from the nose centre.

**Evidence (contributor's Tormach PathPilot Hub 8L conversational samples, used as behaviour reference only):**
- `facing.nc`: a standard OD turning tool, "Tool on X+ side", is **Tool Orientation = 3**. It faces to centre with no complaint, while #640's fit table refuses 3 for facing.
- The OD threading sample wants orientation **8** where #640's table reads an OD thread tip as 6, (-X, 0).
- The chamfer refusals list [1,5,6] / [2,6,7] while the tool was 3 (to be reconciled).

**Reading:** the chart's numbers are drawn in a screen frame. On a rear-tool lathe the frame is mirrored in X: 1↔4, 2↔3, 6↔8, and 5, 7, 9 are unchanged. The physical tip offset of an OD tool is the same (-X, -Z) in machine coordinates either way. Only the **number** changes. So a PathPilot user who enters 3 (their tool table's number) gets the (+X, -Z) offset in #640: posted 2r wrong on diameter, and refused on facing.

**Expected:**
- A machine states its turret side (front or rear).
- The orientation number is read in that machine's frame, so built-in Lathe (front) 2 and Tormach 8L/15L (rear) 3 both mean the standard OD tool.
- Defaults follow the frame: OD insert 2 or 3, boring bar 3 or 2.
- The fit rule and the post's `ORIENTATION q` note use the machine's numbers.
- #641's blade corners (1/2/6) get the same treatment.

**Done means:**
- the three PathPilot data points above reproduce: a facing with 3 on a rear machine passes, an OD thread asks for 8, and the chamfer sets match;
- front-lathe behaviour and goldens are unchanged;
- a rear-machine golden is pinned.

**Blocks** #626 (PathPilot lathe post) and the Tormach lathe machines from relying on orientation numbers. Related: #630/#640, #641/#644, #647.

title: Lathe travel check judges world X, not the turning radius or the posted control point

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while widening the built-in Lathe's X floor for #630 (PR #640).

**Today:** the machine travel check compares each move's world X with the lathe's X band. The turning kernels put their radius on the **Y** meridian (a cached facing path is (0, y, z)), so on those paths the X band never sees the turning radius, whether nose centre or control point. A lathe X over-travel along the Y meridian is never judged by the stroke check. (Thread arcs in XY *are* seen, which is how #631 surfaced.) It also judges the cache (nose centre), not the posted control point that #640 now writes.

**Expected:** for lathe machines, the stroke check judges the **posted** position: the radius on the path's meridian (X or Y, the same way `nose_tip::control_point_path` reads it), shifted to the control point, against the X band; Z against the Z band. An over-travel is refused by name.

**Done means:** a facing path on the Y meridian that runs past the X floor is refused by name. A control point (not the nose centre) at the band edge decides it. Existing lathe goldens and suites stay green.

Related: #630/#640 (control point), #631/#643 (spindle-axis arcs).

title: M7.3: carried stock (the two-sided Body) on the field engine - prerequisite for #586/#589

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while working #586 (M7.3 3/6). Part of #26.

**Why #586 can't finish as a seam move:** every app stock *holder* is either a plain grid or the **carried `Body`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry.rs`). `Body` stores the stock carried between setups as **two-sided columns**: `pub dex: Dexel` plus a per-column floor (`on_floor` / `on_mesh`). It supports the setup-change transforms that `LatticeTurn` makes exact on a lattice: XY quarter turns, Z flips and mirrors (`carry`, `deviate`'s Z-mirror via `Dexel::from_grid`, `display()`).

The app also **mutates** it as a column store:
- `simulate(&mut body.dex, ..)` in `rest/across.rs` and `rest.rs`;
- `stock_sim_carry`'s clip loop writing `dex.lower(..)`;
- `Held::Plain(Dexel)` / `Held::Carried(Body)` and `dex_mut()`.

Swapping `Dexel` for `Stock` there is a **data-model change**: carried stock on the field engine.

**Open design questions:**
1. **Representation:** the field engine holds a solid as a narrow-band SDF plus cut layers. Carrying it is a rigid transform of the field (a re-sample, or a transformed query frame) rather than a lattice permutation. Is a transformed query frame (no re-sample) exact enough for the verdicts?
2. **Floors:** a flipped part's floor is the former top. The field is a closed solid, so it has no separate floor, but "a column cut through" needs an equivalent read.
3. **Clipping** to a later setup's own stock: a field intersection (max of SDFs) replaces `lower`.
4. **Equivalence:** a heavy-lane agreement test of the carried verdicts (`setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups`, `carried_verify`) on both engines, like `stock_engine_agreement`.

**Done means:** `stock_sim_carry`, `rest`, `rest/across` and the operation priors hold carried stock as `Stock`. A field-engine carry passes the same carried-stock suites, plus an agreement lane against the column carry. #586 can then close. This is a prerequisite of #589.

Related: #26, #585 (PR #595), #586, #589, #633 (PR #636, the field block speed fix this depends on).

4. **Post:** a PathPilot plasma post, and whether PathPilot plasma differs from the mill dialect beyond the torch words.
5. **Safety laws:** what replaces the gouge and collision checks (torch height and part tip-up are the real hazards).

**Next step:** answer these from Tormach's 1300PL manual (the contributor can supply it) and public LinuxCNC plasma docs, then file concrete sub-issues per the needs-research process.

title: Setups page: the part-alignment angle Apply turns about the bounds centre (shifts the part relative to the origin); and should 'lay a face on a plane' default to face-down?

body:
Split from #330's reopen report (PR #603 fixed the reachable-controls part).

1. **Angle Apply:** the Part alignment row's typed-angle **Apply** turns the part about its bounds centre, so the part moves relative to the WCS origin. The maintainer's report said the alignment "shifts the model relative to the origin". Decide the pivot: the WCS origin, the bounds centre, or a choice, record it, and make the row say which.
2. **Default Flip:** unflipped currently means the picked face's outside points along +axis, so a face picked on G17 lays outside-up with the part below the plane. Users probably expect the picked face to become the bottom (face-down onto the table). Consider flipping the default; this is the maintainer's call.
3. **Structural test:** `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` asserts the controls are inside the window, not the properties pane rect. Tighten it to the pane rect, so a control spilling past the pane edge (the #330 bug) fails the test.

**Done means:** each item is decided and recorded, with tests where behaviour changes.

title: Setup alignment: set the part's X and Y axis directions by picking an edge or two points

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Proposed by the maintainer (filed by an agent), 2026-11-09: picking the "Y" axis by either an edge or two points, and then X as well, should be an option for aligning parts to the WCS.

**What:** a setup alignment mode that orients the part *within* the work plane, after (or independently of) laying it flat:
- **Y axis:** pick a straight edge, or two points; their direction becomes the setup's +Y (the user can flip the sense).
- **X axis:** the same, by an edge or two points. When both are picked, X is projected so X and Y stay perpendicular (Y wins, or the user picks which is primary; record the choice). When only one is picked, the other follows from the work-plane normal (right-handed: X = Y × Z).
- The axes are measured in the work plane (projected onto it), so a slightly tilted edge still gives a clean in-plane direction. A direction too close to the plane normal is refused by name.

**Relation to the other alignment work:**
- #330 (reopened): face to plane sets the *plane* (which way is down). This sets the *in-plane rotation* (which way X/Y point), so together they give a full part frame.
- #554 drops edge picking for *plane* alignment on the setup page, because an edge can't define a plane. Edges are valid here, because an edge does define a direction. The setup page should make clear which pick each mode takes (face for plane; edge or two points for an axis), so the face pick no longer fights edge snapping.
- #555: three points define a plane (and optionally a full frame from points 1 and 2). This mode can share its point-picking UI and apply path.
- The result applies to the part alignment (#326/#341) and leaves G54-G59 coming from the setup (one WCS per setup).

**Requirements:** one undoable command, validated at creation. Refused by name: a degenerate direction (zero length, two identical points), X and Y parallel, a direction along the plane normal, non-finite input. Undo restores the previous alignment.

**Done means:** tests for an edge at 30 degrees in the plane picked as Y rotating the part so that edge runs along +Y; two points picked as X doing the same for X; both picked giving perpendicular axes per the recorded rule; the degenerate and parallel cases refused by name; and undo/redo walking it.

title: Post: probing on a machine with an inverted X/Y axis (refused by name since #374)

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Part of #372. #374 refuses probing (TOUCH / RETREAT / FOUND records) by name on a machine with an inverted axis: `operation <op>: probing is not supported for an inverted axis yet`.

Why it was refused rather than translated: the Fanuc/Haas probing blocks run in the controller's frame through macro code: the G31 skip, the `#5061..` trip variables, the no-contact check against the target, the incremental G91 back-off (`DeltaX/Y/Z`), the deviation `found - expected` and the `G10 L2` work-offset write. The mirror rule would negate the target, expected point, back-off delta and `Axes[].Expected` on the inverted axis. But the #374 equivalence reader models motion only, not the macro arithmetic, so nothing would pin the translation.

Done means: `invert.rs` translates TOUCH/RETREAT/FOUND for an inverted X/Y (target, expect, delta, per-axis Expected). A test interprets the posted probing blocks with a simulated trip on the inverted controller and checks that the offset written to the work-offset register is the physical correction. The refusal is lifted for Fanuc and Haas only.
